request: the design misses timing at 200 MHz: improve its timing

options.title: Carry-select split of the s_reg adder
options.approach: In montgomery_core, split the 64-bit add that feeds s_reg into a low and a high half. Compute the high half for carry-in 0 and 1, and pick the result with the carry out of the low half. This roughly halves the 18-CARRY4 chain on the worst path, s_reg[1]_replica to s_reg[64]. The W+2 clock latency, the ports and the other components are not changed.

gain.basis_note: The path has 18 CARRY4 levels in a 5.59 ns data path. Halving the chain should remove a good part of the carry delay, but I have no per-cell delays, so this range is a guess. The low end is the slack needed to close timing.

cost.note: One RTL change, then route. The mux on the carry and the other near-critical paths among the 33 failing endpoints may need a second round.
cost.basis: iterations are the generator's estimate (a guess); no recorded build time, so no wall-time figure

options.title: Carry-save accumulator in the multiplier loop
options.approach: In montgomery_core, keep s in carry-save form (sum and carry vectors) inside the bit-serial loop, so the loop has no carry chain across 64 bits. Resolve the carry only once at the end, with a final add that must fit inside the fixed W+2 clocks. The register window and top are not changed.

gain.basis_note: The 18 CARRY4 levels dominate the worst path, and a carry-save loop removes them, so the gain could be large. The final resolving add may become the new critical path, so the range is a guess. The high end stays within half of the 5.0 ns period.

cost.note: Larger RTL rewrite. The final carry resolution has to be fitted into the fixed latency, and the design has to be re-verified.

options.title: Synthesis and placement strategy exploration
options.approach: Leave the RTL unchanged and rerun synthesis and implementation with timing-oriented strategies, such as performance-explore directives and post-route physical optimisation. Try a few strategies and keep the best result. Routing is only about a quarter of the worst path, so only a small gain is expected.

gain.basis_note: Routing is 26.4% of the 5.59 ns data path, about 1.5 ns, and the carry chain is fixed logic. A strategy change can recover only part of the routing share, so the range is a guess and may not reach the 0.615 ns needed.

cost.note: Each strategy is one full build. No RTL is changed.
